raw_response:
I'm 63 this year. Been farming since I was 23 — that's 40 years on this land in Quzhou. Never went to school, can't read the numbers on the fertilizer bags, but I know my fields. It's just me and my old man now, two of us working 16 mu and a bit. We don't have much cash to throw around, so every yuan has to count.

Our land is split into two pieces: about 10 mu for wheat then maize, same as most folks around here, and the other 6 mu or so in cotton. I plant cotton because if grain prices are bad one year, at least the cotton gives us something different to sell. But cotton is hand-work from start to finish, and with just two of us getting old, it's getting harder.

The wheat went in last October around the 10th, like it always does. I used our own seed, kept from the harvest before — big plump kernels, no need to buy. I put down base fertilizer then, about one big 50-jin bag of that compound stuff for every two and a half mu. Now it's late April, the wheat is up and jointing. I already walked the fields in late March and spread urea by hand, about 15 jin per mu. That's what I've always done. Old Zhang down the lane tried cutting back on fertilizer two years ago to save money, and his wheat came up like straw — thin and yellow. I won't make that mistake. Better to spend a bit more than risk losing the crop. I'll irrigate three times total: once already at green-up, once when it heads in May, and maybe once more when it fills if the weather turns dry. The pump electricity keeps getting dearer, so I watch every watering.

We harvest the wheat in early June with the hired combine — costs about 50 yuan per mu, but we're too old to swing a scythe now. Then we got barely a day or two to turn around and get the maize in the ground. I always buy new hybrid seed for maize — can't save it, doesn't work the second year. About 4 jin per mu. I put compound fertilizer down with the planter when we seed, then topdress with urea once when the maize is knee-high. Summer rains usually help, so I only irrigate once or twice, depending on how July goes. If it's a dry summer, I'll water; if it rains, I save the pump money.

Cotton goes in the ground in late April on the other 6 mu. Bt cotton, I buy new seed every year. I plow that plot with a hired tractor — we don't have one big enough. For fertilizer, I put less on cotton than on grain: about one bag of compound for the whole 6 mu, and maybe a handful of urea when it flowers. I irrigate twice — once after planting if the spring is dry, and once when it's flowering. I spray for weeds and whatever bugs show up. Even Bt cotton needs some spraying. The picking goes on for weeks, September into October. With just two of us, we hire a few women from the village to help at picking time, pay them by the day.

Money is tight. We buy what we need, but nothing fancy. No new machines, no "precision" anything. I use round numbers, what my eyes tell me, and what has put food on the table for four decades. My neighbor with the high school diploma talks about soil tests and optimal rates — I just know that 15 jin of urea per mu of wheat has never let me down.
